title: test(app-shell,console): approvals and inbox reads carry the console's UI language
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgTACWfLyuZEQ4gVESvk5YRQ)_

Part of #37483

## What changes

Test-only. Two pins hold every approvals reader and the notification inbox read to the console's authenticated fetch, which sends the active UI language as `Accept-Language`:

- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/approvalsUiLocale-37483.test.tsx`: the approval history read (`listApprovalActions`, `/approvals/requests/:id/actions`), `remindApprovalRequest`, `fetchPendingApprovalPage` (bell, home, full-page inbox), and the notification inbox: the real `AdapterProvider` mounted with `useSharedInboxFeed`, asserting the header on its `sys_inbox_message` read.
- `ui/apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.uiLocale-37483.test.tsx`: the request page's history (`sys_approval_action` timeline) and request read (`process_label` / `step_label`) through `routeApprovalRecordReads(adapter)`, as `AppContent` wires it.

Each pin sets `<html lang="en">` and asserts `Accept-Language: en`. The controls are on the stamp itself: an empty `<html lang>` adds no header rather than a guessed one.

## Why

The card was measured on the 18.6.0 bundles. On `main` the shared helper the card suggests already does the job: `createAuthenticatedFetch` (`@object-ui/auth`) stamps `<html lang>` as `Accept-Language` on every `/api/` call, and the readers it names now go through it:

- `useRecordApprovals` (`fetchJson`: request, actions, remind) and `sharedUserFeeds` (`fetchPendingApprovalPage`) moved from a bare `fetch` + `bearerAuthHeaders()` to it in #37185 (merged 2026-11-25, after 18.6.0).
- `approvalsApi.ts` and `approvalRequestsDataSource.ts` have used it since #27040 / #28619.
- The inbox (`sys_inbox_message`, `sys_notification_receipt`) reads through the console adapter, which `AdapterProvider` builds on the same fetch.

So no source change is needed for approval history; what was missing is a pin that keeps these surfaces on that transport. Ablation: replacing the stamp in `createAuthenticatedFetch` with a no-op turns all six positive pins red, controls stay green; building `AdapterProvider`'s adapter on a bare `fetch` turns the inbox pin red.

**Why `Part of`, not `Fixes`:** the inbox read already went through the stamped adapter at 18.6.0, so "fixed after 18.6.0" does not explain the inbox evidence in comment 7186322473. The card stays open until a header capture of `GET /api/v1/data/sys_inbox_message` on a `main` build settles it (reported on the card).

## Verification

- `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/approvalsUiLocale-37483.test.tsx apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.uiLocale-37483.test.tsx`: 9 passed.
- Ablations above: 6 failed / 3 passed with the stamp removed; inbox pin red with the adapter on a bare `fetch`.
- `eslint` on both files: clean. `check:commit-card-trailers`, `overlap-check`: clean.

Publishes nothing (test files only), so `skip-changeset`.
